messages:
Priya (CS): FYI we completed Tidepool's private VPC dry run. Found three blockers: CIDR conflict, customer-managed KMS key access, and log forwarding to their Datadog endpoint failing with 401s. Customer flags this as a deal risk for next-week renewal. Need owners & P0 triage.
Marco (NetEng): Share the exact CIDRs they plan to use? I can check overlap and propose a subnet carve or transit gateway option.
Priya (CS): They insisted on 172.16.0.0/16 for their VPC. Our standard stacks assume 172.20.0.0/16. They cannot renumber this quarter due to carrier NAT constraints.
Marco (NetEng): Unfortunate. Options: 1) Use our side carveout + strict routing (no overlap), 2) Transit GW with route translation, or 3) deploy NAT/proxy in a non-overlapping management VPC. Option 3 is fastest but adds NAT hops and egress cost. I'll sketch latency impact.
Lena (Security): For KMS: customer wants customer-managed CMK with key policy denying account root and only allowing an explicit role. Our service needs sts:AssumeRole into a role in their account and then kms:Decrypt. We need their role ARN and a statement in the CMK key policy allowing the assumed role.
Priya (CS): They sent role ARN: arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/Tidepool-Redwood-Role. However their role trust policy currently allows only their CI principal. They won't permit wildcard assume.
Marco (NetEng): @Lena what's the minimal cross-account trust they must add so our service can assume it (one-liner)?
Lena (Security): Minimal trust policy to paste to Tidepool (they should replace PRINCIPAL with our service role ARN):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-service"},
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
    }
  ]
}
```
Lena (Security): Also their CMK key policy must include a Statement granting kms:Decrypt to the above role ARN (not the root). I'll paste a minimal key policy snippet into the ticket.
ops-bot: Log forward attempt recorded 2026-03-22T09:14Z: Datadog HTTP response 401 Unauthorized. Payload: "api_key_invalid". Forwarder used role arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/Tidepool-LogPush. See /var/log/forwarder/2026-03-22-0914.log
Priya (CS): So two IAM pieces: (A) role for Redwood to assume for KMS decrypt; (B) role/policy that the forwarder uses must include datadog:PostSeries (or appropriate Put) and their API key needs to be valid. They reported rotating the key yesterday; could be mismatch.
Marco (NetEng): For the CIDR, if renumbering is impossible, I prefer Transit GW + routing isolations — cleaner long-term and supports peering to multiple customers without NAT. Short-term we can spin up a proxy NAT in our management VPC. I'll estimate infra hours + monthly cost.
Priya (CS): Renewal risk: customer said if we can't guarantee private-only paths (no traffic transiting public ranges) they may ask legal pauses. We must escalate. Mark as P0.
infra-bot: Created ticket CUS-9123: "Tidepool private VPC blockers (CIDR, KMS, logs)" assigned to Marco and Lena. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CUS-9123
Oliver (CS Manager): I'll join triage and loop in renewals/legal. Can we have a short internal sync tomorrow 10:30am PT to align ask list before we send to Tidepool?
Priya (CS): Yes — scheduling now. Action items: Marco to propose network workaround + cost; Lena to draft exact IAM and CMK policy snippets for customer; Marco/Lena to add minimal verification steps. I'll prepare customer update draft after internal sync.
Marco (NetEng): Noted — will upload network diagram and latency estimate to CUS-9123 by EOD today.
Lena (Security): Will provide policy snippets and a small test checklist (assume role test, kms:Decrypt smoke test, datadog push test) in the ticket.
Priya (CS): Thanks team. Tidepool expects an update before their renewal call next Wednesday. I'll include owner names and ETA in the customer-facing note. :eyes:
